concept.concept_description: Formalize 'strange loops' — hierarchical levels that fold back on themselves. Define: a strange loop in a formal system F is a formula phi such that phi asserts its own provability or unprovability. Prove: Gödel's incompleteness theorem IS a strange loop (the Gödel sentence G says 'G is not provable'). Show: Tarski's undefinability of truth is a stronger strange loop (no formula can assert its own truth). Conjecture: every sufficiently expressive formal system contains infinitely many distinct strange loops. Explore: can we formalize the 'tangled hierarchy' where level N refers to level N-1 which refers to level N?
